newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close down on profit-taking.

text.p: Delhi stock prices fell back to close lower on selling by profit-takers, dealers said on Wednesday, though buying by foreign institutional investors earlier in the day had kept prices up.
Brokers said the early highs followed the new Congress chief Sitaram Kesri's avowal of the party's continued support to the United Front coalition.
But the FIIs continued to buy shares of the State Bank of India and ITC Ltd, which closed higher.
"FIIs were aggressive buyers particularly in State Bank of India and ITC Ltd throughout the session but failed to enthuse the sentiment," said Jagdish Grover of brokers Multiple Investments.
The Delhi Stock Exchange indicative index ended 1.82 points lower at 737.31 points.

Indian commerce secretary Tejendra Khanna's statement that the country has been facing an economic slowdown in fiscal 1996-97 (April/March), caused some worry among marketmen who preferred to take a cautious approach.

Reliance ended a shade higher at 197.15 rupees off the day's high of 200.10, but selling by profit-takers wiped out early gains. Shares of SBI, the country's largest public sector bank, gained 1.45 rupees at 264.50 on heavy purchases by FIIs ahead of the pricing of its Euroissue, expected early in October.
ITC Ltd firmed 1.40 rupees at 299.80 after rallying to 303.75 rupees on FIIs' heavy purchases.

TISCO dropped 0.95 rupees at 173 rupees, Larsen and Toubro 2.10 rupees at 240.10, Asian Hotels 11.05 rupees at 272, BSES Ltd 1.75 rupees at 177.50, Oriental Bank of Commerce 0.70 rupees to 21.10. ACC fell 27 rupees to 1849 and TELCO 1.65 rupees at 458.60.
